𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽 𝗶𝘀𝗻’𝘁 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗯𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀—𝗶𝘁’𝘀 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝗳𝗹𝘂𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲, 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁. 
Here’s how to use NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming) to lead like a pro:

1️⃣ 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵 & 𝗠𝗶𝗿𝗿𝗼𝗿 🤝 – People trust those who "get" them. Subtly mirror body language and tone to build instant rapport.

2️⃣ 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗖𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱𝘀 🗣️ – Swap “You must” for “What if we…” to inspire action instead of resistance.

3️⃣ 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗹 🧘 – A leader who panics spreads chaos. Master your emotions, and your team will mirror your calm confidence.

4️⃣ 𝗥𝗲𝗳𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗴𝗲𝘀 🔄 – Instead of “We have a problem,” say “We have an opportunity to get creative.” Energy shifts instantly!

5️⃣ 𝗔𝘀𝗸, 𝗗𝗼𝗻’𝘁 𝗔𝘀𝘀𝘂𝗺𝗲 ❓ – Powerful questions unlock solutions. “How do you see this?” gets more buy-in than “Do this.”

6️⃣ 𝗔𝗰𝘁 ‘𝗔𝘀 𝗜𝗳’ 🎭 – Want respect? Show up as the leader your team needs, even before you feel 100% ready.

7️⃣ 𝗖𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗯𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗠𝗶𝗰𝗿𝗼-𝗪𝗶𝗻𝘀 🎉 – A simple “I see the effort you put in” fuels motivation 10x more than generic praise.

Leadership isn’t about control—it’s about connection. Master these, and watch your team rise with you. 🚀

Ever made a snap decision and later thought, “What was I thinking?!” 🤦‍♂️ 

We often believe decision-making is purely instinctive, but in reality, it’s a skill that can be trained and refined—just like learning to play chess or mastering a sport. And this is where Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP) comes in!

NLP helps rewire the way we think, process information, and ultimately make smarter choices. Here’s how:

1. 𝗥𝗲𝗳𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴: 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝗦𝗲𝗲 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 🔄🔍
A bad decision isn’t failure—it’s feedback. NLP teaches us to reframe situations so we learn rather than regret.
✅ 𝗘𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲: Instead of thinking, “I made the wrong business move,” reframe it as, “Now I know what doesn’t work, and I’m closer to what does.”

2. 𝗠𝗲𝘁𝗮 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹: 𝗔𝘀𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗤𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 ❓💡
Our decisions are only as good as the information we have. NLP’s Meta Model helps break down vague thoughts into clear, actionable insights.
✅ 𝗘𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲: If your brain says, “I can’t do this,” challenge it:
👉 “What specifically is stopping me? What resources do I need? Who has done this before?”
By asking better questions, you get better answers—and better decisions.

𝟯. 𝗙𝘂𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗣𝗮𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗴: 𝗧𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗕𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 🚀🔮
Future pacing is like a mental “time machine” where you visualize the outcome of your choice before making it.
✅ 𝗘𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲: Before launching a product, mentally walk through:
👉 “If I go this route, how will it play out in 6 months? What obstacles might come up? How would I handle them?”

This reduces impulsive decisions and boosts strategic thinking.

🏆🏆🏆🏆🏆
Good decision-making isn’t about luck—it’s about training your brain to think critically and strategically. With NLP techniques like reframing, the Meta Model, and future pacing, you can transform the way you approach choices.

So, what’s one decision you can make smarter today? 🤔👇

NLP isn’t just about persuasion—it’s about rewiring how you process information, spot patterns, and make razor-sharp decisions. Here are three game-changing NLP techniques to help you think smarter and strategize better.

𝟭. 𝗥𝗲𝗳𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴: 𝗦𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗣𝗶𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝗮 𝗡𝗲𝘄 𝗟𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 🖼️🔍
In business, setbacks are inevitable. But is it really a failure… or just feedback? Reframing helps you flip the script and see opportunities where others see problems.
🔹 Example 1: Imagine you are running a startup, and a major client suddenly pulls out. Instead of panicking ("We're doomed!"), you reframe:
👉 “This opens up space for better clients who align with our vision.”

2. 𝗖𝗵𝘂𝗻𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴: 𝗭𝗼𝗼𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗜𝗻 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗢𝘂𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗦𝗺𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 🔄🎯

🔹 Example 1: Let’s say you are launching a new product, but the details are overwhelming. Instead of drowning in endless to-do lists, ask:

🔹 Example 1: You admire Elon Musk’s ability to innovate. Instead of just reading about him, ask:
👉 “How does he approach problem-solving? What questions does he ask? What assumptions does he challenge?”

It’s like borrowing a successful blueprint rather than guessing your way forward. The fastest path to success? Think like those who’ve already cracked the code. 🔑

media.title: The #1 NLP Technique to Make People Agree with You Without Resistance ...
media.caption:
The #1 NLP Technique to Make People Agree with You Without Resistance 🤝✨

Ever had a conversation where you are trying to convince someone, but they just won’t budge? It’s like trying to push a mountain with a toothpick! ⛰️😂 Well, here’s an NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming) trick that flips the script—Pacing & Leading.

🚶‍♂️ Pace First, Lead L𝗮𝘁𝗲r
Instead of shoving your opinion down someone’s throat (which, let’s be real, never works), you meet them where they are first. This means you align with their thoughts, emotions, or behaviours before gently guiding them in your direction.
✅ 𝗘𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲:
Imagine you are at a dinner party, and someone says, “I think pineapple on pizza is a crime!” 🍕🚫 Instead of instantly saying, “No way, it’s amazing!” (which triggers defensiveness), you start by pacing:

👉 “I get why you’d feel that way—fruit on a pizza? It does sound weird at first.” 🎯

Now they feel heard. Then, you lead:

👉 “But, you know, the sweetness with the cheese kinda works—it’s like a tropical flavor explosion!” 💥

By validating their perspective first, you reduce resistance, making them more open to your viewpoint.

🧠 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗜𝘁 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
People resist when they feel opposed, but they open up when they feel understood. Pacing builds rapport, lowers defences, and makes your words feel like a natural extension of their thoughts.

So next time you want to influence someone (without the drama), pace, then lead! 🏆

Leadership isn’t just about strategy—it’s about emotional mastery. When pressure rises, emotions can cloud judgment.

Here’s how to stay cool, clear, and in control using NLP:

𝟭. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗣𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗔𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗿: 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗖𝗮𝗹𝗺 𝗼𝗻 𝗗𝗲𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗱
Imagine a moment when you felt completely in control. Close your eyes, relive it vividly—see, hear, feel it. Now, press your thumb and forefinger together. Repeat daily. When stress hits, use this anchor to trigger instant calm.

Ever felt a surge of frustration in a meeting? Or that lump in your throat before a tough conversation? Emotions at work are real, but they don’t have to rule you. NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming) gives you the tools to stay cool, composed, and in control.

𝟭. 𝗔𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗿 𝗬𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗳𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲
Think of a time you felt unstoppable. Now, press two fingers together while reliving that moment. Do this often, and soon, that simple touch will trigger instant confidence when you need it most.

𝟮. 𝗥𝗲𝗳𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗬𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀
Stuck in a stressful situation? Instead of saying, “This is a disaster,” try, “This is a challenge I can handle.” Words shape emotions. Choose wisely.

𝟯. 𝗠𝗶𝗿𝗿𝗼𝗿 & 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗕𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗹
Dealing with an aggressive coworker? Subtly match their posture and tone (not mockingly, just slightly). This builds subconscious rapport and shifts the energy.

Meet Maya and Arjun. Both are managers at different companies, and both faced the same challenge—a difficult conversation with a highly opinionated, often confrontational team member. Let’s see how they handled it.

𝗠𝗮𝘆𝗮’𝘀 𝗔𝗽𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵: The Emotional Rollercoaster
Maya walked into the meeting room tense, her heart racing. 

She had rehearsed all the ways she would defend herself if things got heated. The moment Rahul, her team member, began criticizing a project decision, Maya felt attacked.
Her voice sharpened, “I don’t think you understand the full picture!”

Rahul crossed his arms. “Well, I don’t think you’re listening to your team.”

The conversation spiraled. Maya was frustrated, Rahul was defensive, and nothing was resolved. She left the room exhausted, questioning her leadership.

𝗔𝗿𝗷𝘂𝗻’𝘀 𝗔𝗽𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵: 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗡𝗟𝗣 𝗪𝗮𝘆
Arjun, on the other hand, prepared differently. Before the meeting, he used Anchoring, recalling a time when he felt calm and confident. He tapped his wrist, reinforcing the emotion.

As soon as he sat down with Rohan (a similarly difficult team member), he Mirrored his posture slightly, matching his tone to build rapport.

When Rohan began venting, Arjun used Reframing, responding with, “I hear you. It sounds like you’re really passionate about this. Let’s explore a solution together.”
This simple shift changed the energy in the room. Arjun also used Meta-Model Questions, digging deeper. “What specifically concerns you about this decision?”

Rohan, feeling understood, softened. The conversation ended with a constructive action plan. Arjun left feeling in control, not drained.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗩𝗲𝗿𝗱𝗶𝗰𝘁? 𝗡𝗟𝗣 𝗪𝗶𝗻𝘀.
Maya let emotions control her, while Arjun controlled the emotions in the room. Difficult conversations are inevitable, but with NLP, they don’t have to be battles—they can be bridges.

The result? The distance melted away. A boy once retreating under constant reprimands now leaned in, listened, and responded.

media.title: Here are the ten game-changing habits for deeper conversations.  1. Li...
media.caption:
Here are the ten game-changing habits for deeper conversations.

1. Listen more. Ask more. Try to know more about the other person.

2. Even if the person is sharing an incident that may be draining their energies too, prompt them to notice positives rather than abruptly changing the topic.

3. Remember, it is a conversation, not a debate. Being judgemental or having strong disagreements is not your outcome.

4. Respect, don't impost. Suggest, don't bombard.

5. Praise the tiny but real things in the other person.

6. Embrace the differences and celebrate them.

7. Don't dominate the discussion, also don't be an absolute mute. Bring balance.

8. Don't overthink before sharing.

9. Ask deep questions like, 'What drives you in life?' and 'What made you bring this change in life?'

10. Don't be critical of what others say. They, too, have the right to express their opinions like you do.

media.caption:
Validation- to look for or not to look for?
Well, whether to look for it or not, here are the ways you can give authentic validation. 
1. Ask questions to show interest. Notice their body language. It will give them the feeling of being heard.

2. Reflect through paraphrasing what the other person is saying. It is like becoming their soundboard to help them think better.

3. When you read their behaviour, you look for alignment in their thoughts and actions without being judgemental. The key here is to bring it to their notice for their own good, not to showcase your observational skills.

4. Make them feel heard by saying, "I know you", "I got you" as you have been with them In past. 

5. Normalise their action by acknowledging that in such situation, it was ok. 

6. Listen to understand with radical genuineness. Don't just listen to bombard advice.

2. Ask and don't assume- Often the personal hurt comes from the vague assumptions. The quickest hack is to ask them what they mean rather than connecting the dots by yourself.

3. Setting healtny boundaries- Limit negative people and tap into only supportive circle.

4. Practice self-compassion- Acknowledge your feelings, but don't dwell on negativity.

5. Know your self-worth- When your skin is thick, no comment can cut through. Your self-worth is your ultimate weapon.

media.title: What if Creativity was a magic potion? All you needed to do was pour a...
media.caption:
What if Creativity was a magic potion? All you needed to do was pour a spoonful into your brain daily and get going? Imagine the Creative syrup dissolving into your blood and veins and making its way to each organ of your body. How different your life would have been? How would it intersect with your work? Or how would it restructure you as a human being? Moreover, how would it affect your day-to-day decisions and beliefs?

Never gave it much thought? Fret not!
The first belief we must smash is “Creativity is only needed at work.” 

What about convincing a child to have a glass of milk by matching his thoughts and moulding your talks accordingly? What if you choose not to go on the highway or your own way? 

When we say, ‘Creativity is thinking outside the box,’ we fail to realize that we are boxing Creativity this way. 

The unsaid rule is that Creativity is a multi-purpose Swiss military knife, which can be used to slice, chop, cut, split, and smash issues springing up in various spheres of your life. 

Time to sprinkle the spiritual tadka!

As everything is energy and energy is everything, Creativity is also an energy zone we can keep tapping into. How?

Well, I have an ABC RULE OF CREATIVE ENERGY.

A- ASK- Keep asking questions, not to others, but to yourself. One of the best questions to ask is- ‘WHAT IF’. E.g., WHAT IF I could do this task differently? 
For example, what if there is another way out, and I never thought about it? 
For example, what if this is true/false? 
More questions can be a combination of open-ended and close-ended questions like- 
•	What is this situation telling/teaching me?
•	What is it making me feel? (labelling the emotion)
•	Where is this thought coming from? (checking origin)
 Questions like these will be your oar to cross the ocean of self-discovery. 

B- BREAK RULES- Breaking the rules is just tweaking the patterns. How?
•	Changing the sequence of your book arrangement on the bookshelf opens your mind to think broader and expand the horizons of other possibilities for doing the same thing.
 (CONTD IN COMMENTS)

media.caption:
Dear Diwali, 

You may not know me, but I am getting to know you better. Since I am called ‘Neuro Linguistic Programming’, A Study of Subjective Experiences, I am choosing to know you subjectively. 

With time, your meaning has changed and so has the internal representation of you in people’s minds. From being a religious festival to also being a medium to chill out or take family vacations, your submodalities have shifted drastically. For some you are the time to decorate homes and cook delicacies, for others you mean a break from work, for some you are a good change and for a few, you also might be a festival they dread because they lost someone during these days. 

With this roller-coaster of meaning-making cycles, you have always had your behaviour flexibility while upholding your outcome orientation of bringing a sense of joy. 

So no matter how simple or distorted you have become in people’s minds, you have chosen to stay in the ‘cause’ mode by bringing people together, and also passing on this state to all so they could inhale the same joy. 

With changing times, something which was considered to be so inherent in you, i.e. crackers, also took a back seat. With your ignited sensory acuity, you inspired the world to get into the cause mode about upcoming pollution disasters. I loved that you were pretty cool about being labelled as ‘Green Diwali’ or eco-friendly Diwali. 

You have anchored yourself in people’s minds to the fundamental emotions of love, light and togetherness across all the neurological levels of change, whether it is environment, behaviour, capabilities, beliefs and values. What remained same and will always be your purpose of drawing a sketch of luminous love and light and your identity as a joyful occasion. 

Glad to know you and live you every year, and especially glad to witness that you have lived me (NLP) so gracefully all these years too.

Thoughtfully Yours,
NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming)

media.title: My Dear Friends,   You will be happy to know that I have been invited ...
media.caption:
My Dear Friends, 

You will be happy to know that I have been invited as a Subject Expert to present my views in the 9th edition of RISE: WORLD SUMMIT 2022.

RWS, is a virtual event from 3rd to 5th February 2022. 

More than 1500 delegates from more than 55 countries will be taking part in this iconic online event. 

The purpose of the event to generate conversation and arrive at actionable conclusions to reach the 17 Sustainable Development Goals to Transform the World by 2030, as set by world nations in September 2015 at the UNO. 

I have been invited to be part of the Roundtable on Financial Literacy: Community Financial Well-being 

The Roundtable discussion will take place on 3rd February 2022, at 11.30 am (IST)

The subject experts in the Round Table along with me are from diverse fields and countries with stellar experience. 

The topic is also very interesting and thought provoking. I am sure my experience will assist me in giving justice to the topic.

Please do join and experience the expertise and diverse world views on this topic. 

Apart from the Roundtable, there are Chat tables too at different times for you to contribute/discuss. 

There are workshops, tours, fests and film screenings (not available on Youtube), and awards, apart from the Planery and Closing Sessions. 

You will need to register on the platform to participate. This will take just 3 minutes. 

Here is the link: 
www.risesummit.in

You will enjoy the inclusive immersive experience. Look forward to your active participation, support and feedback.

- Mehernosh Randeria – Mumbai’s First GTD Trainer

Register NOW at http://www.calmachiever.com/gtd-fundamentals-011/
